content:
I am a researcher at Inria and Université Grenoble-Alpes, in the GHOST team in Grenoble, which I joined in July 2025.
My research focuses on the theory of reinforcement learning, with a particular interest in posterior sampling and policy gradient methods. I study the exploration and optimization properties of these methods to understand when and how efficiently they learn. My interests also include multi-armed bandits and online learning.

title: Students

summary: We separate the decision to explore from the choice of an exploration policy in posterior-sampling RL, taking a step toward instance-dependent regret optimality.
title: Towards instance-dependent regret optimality in Episodic MDPs with Posterior Sampling

authors: Jorge C. Berny Mier y Teran
summary: We analyze an international coffee trial to understand how climate shapes varietal performance, yield stability and resistance to coffee leaf rust.
title: An international multilocation trial reveals genotype-by-environment interactions in Arabica coffee across climate gradients

summary: We bound the finite-time error and bias of coupled stochastic-approximation algorithms, showing how nonlinear dynamics and the two step sizes interact.
title: The Bias of Nonlinear Two-Time-scale Stochastic Approximation under Constant Step-Sizes

summary: We show how a perturbation scheme connects unconstrained linear bandits to online linear optimization, yielding guarantees for fixed and changing comparators.
title: A Perturbation Approach to Unconstrained Linear Bandits

summary: We characterize how the learning rate determines whether stochastic-gradient bandits achieve logarithmic regret or can suffer polynomial regret.
title: Does Stochastic Gradient really succeed for bandits?

summary: We study bandit convex optimization in changing environments and develop regret guarantees under several measures of non-stationarity.
title: Non-stationary Bandit Convex Optimization: A Comprehensive Study

summary: We study when to pay for feedback in contextual bandits, with algorithms that adapt to both stochastic and adversarial environments.
title: Best-of-Both Worlds for linear contextual bandits with paid observations

summary: We exploit the structure of multi-unit uniform-price auctions to improve learning guarantees under limited feedback.
title: Improved learning rates in multi-unit uniform price auctions

summary: We quantify how advance information about future rewards can improve reinforcement learning, from immediate reward lookahead to full reward information.
title: The Value of Reward Lookahead in Reinforcement Learning

summary: We study optimal stopping when rejected items can be revisited at a reduced value, and characterize how this changes prophet-inequality guarantees.
title: Lookback Prophet Inequalities

summary: We model coalition participation in repeated auctions as a structured bandit problem and develop algorithms with constant problem-dependent regret.
title: Optimizing the coalition gain in Online Auctions with Greedy Structured Bandits

summary: We use risk-aware bandit learning to identify fertilizer practices while reducing farmers' yield losses during agricultural trials.
title: A new adaptive identification strategy of best crop management with farmers

summary: We design a bandit algorithm that balances total reward with minimum revenue requirements for every arm, without assuming a known safe policy.
title: Multi-Armed Bandits with Guaranteed Revenue per Arm

summary: We give a common framework for analyzing randomized bandit algorithms, covering Thompson sampling and minimum empirical divergence methods across different reward models.
title: A General Recipe for the Analysis of Randomized Multi-Armed Bandit Algorithms

summary: We make asymptotically optimal non-parametric bandit algorithms more practical by reducing the computational and memory costs of their KL calculations.
title: Fast asymptotically optimal algorithms for non-parametric stochastic bandits

summary: My thesis develops non-parametric bandit algorithms and studies risk-aware exploration, extreme rewards and applications in agriculture.
title: Non-parametric algorithms for Multi-Armed Bandits

summary: We extend the theoretical guarantees of Top Two best-arm identification algorithms beyond Gaussian rewards, including bounded reward distributions.
title: Top Two Algorithms Revisited

summary: We introduce efficient bandit algorithms for finding exceptionally large rewards, using quantiles of maxima to guide exploration.
title: Efficient Algorithms for Extreme Bandits

summary: We develop resampling-based bandit algorithms that combine strong regret guarantees with robustness to uncertain reward distributions.
title: From Optimality to Robustness: Adaptive Re-Sampling Strategies in Stochastic Bandits

summary: We show that deterministic subsampling can achieve optimal bandit exploration with limited memory, and adapt it to changing reward distributions.
title: On Limited-Memory Subsampling Strategies for Bandits

summary: We develop Thompson sampling algorithms that learn to manage downside risk, with optimal asymptotic guarantees for CVaR bandits.
title: Optimal Thompson Sampling strategies for support-aware CVaR bandits

summary: We introduce a resampling-based bandit algorithm that achieves asymptotically optimal exploration across several reward families without distribution-specific tuning.
title: Sub-sampling for Efficient Non-Parametric Bandit Exploration
